rules.statement: When a user-supplied value is spliced into a larger command or script template, validate the fully composed string (parse it and require no errors) or reject tokens such as comments that can swallow the template's surrounding syntax; don't validate only the bare value.
rules.why: A value like `./env.ps1 # note` passes a bare-value check but comments out the closing brace of the wrapper, so the command fails with a parse error that bypasses the intended failure handling.
rules.check: Look for validation functions that parse or inspect only the inserted value while the value is later embedded in a `try { . <value> } ...` or similar template; check that comment tokens, statement separators and stray braces are rejected or the composed string is parsed.

rules.statement: Run the same validation on a value at every entry point that consumes it; don't validate the copy read from one source and execute an equivalent copy from another source unchecked.
rules.why: Otherwise a value that one path reports as invalid runs as written through another path, which breaks the one-rule-for-every-entry-point design.
rules.check: Find every place that reads and executes or splices the value (config file, plan file, alternative runner) and check that each calls the shared validation before use.

rules.statement: When a directive line is present but malformed (wrong quoting, empty value), fail with an error that names the line instead of silently treating the directive as absent.
rules.why: Silently ignoring it runs later commands without the intended setup, and they fail for reasons that point nowhere near the real cause.
rules.check: Look for regex or parser matches on an optional directive where a non-matching but present line just falls through to the no-directive behaviour.

rules.statement: Code that loads a function or type dynamically (by parsing another file, reflection or lookup by name) must throw a clear error naming what it expected when the lookup finds nothing, rather than proceeding with a null result.
rules.why: A lookup that returns null after a rename or a missing file otherwise loads nothing without error, or fails later with an unclear null-reference error.
rules.check: Look for `Find`/`GetType`/`GetMethod`-style lookups whose result is used without a null check and a descriptive throw.

rules.statement: Tests must exercise the production loader or startup path that wires up the code under test, not a test-only reimplementation of that wiring.
rules.why: If the test extracts the functions itself, a broken production loader makes the real script fail at startup while the test stays green.
rules.check: Compare how the test obtains the code under test with how production code loads it; flag tests that duplicate the loading logic instead of calling it.

rules.statement: Test every branch of a failure-detection or validation condition, including the success path and a control case that must not be classified as the failure, not only one failing input.
rules.why: A regression in an untested half of the condition could let a failure through as success or misclassify an ordinary failure, and the suite would stay green.
rules.check: For each guard (compound conditions, operator checks, path checks such as `..`, backslash, absolute or directory paths), check that the tests include an input that hits each branch plus a passing control case.

rules.statement: When adding a new configuration key, add a test that the existing configuration without the key still produces the documented default.
rules.why: Existing projects won't have the key, and a bug that treats it as invalid or empty when missing would break every one of them.
rules.check: For a newly introduced config/setting key, look for a test case where the key is absent and the default value is asserted.

rules.statement: Don't report that a behaviour test runs its own literal copy of a shipped command when the same test also requires that exact full string, verbatim, in every shipped copy.
rules.why: The verbatim check means the shipped command can't drift from the tested one without the test failing, so extracting it from the document adds nothing.
rules.check: Before reporting, check whether the test asserts the whole literal (not just a phrase) is contained in each shipped file.

rules.statement: An error or stop message that states a rule must not contradict its own example; name the forbidden construct precisely (for example 'a leading `.` or `&` operator') rather than an ambiguous character.
rules.why: A message saying 'without a leading `.`' next to the example `./build/env.ps1` can make users strip a correct `./` path prefix.
rules.check: Read new or changed validation messages next to the examples they give and check that the examples satisfy the rule as worded.

rules.statement: When an instruction or check detects a condition by matching command output (for example 'ends with X'), match against the output exactly as the invoking wrapper produces it, including any lines the wrapper appends.
rules.why: If the wrapper always appends an exit-code line, an 'ends with X' rule can never match, so the intended immediate stop never happens.
rules.check: Compare the output-matching condition with the exact command line that produces the output and look for appended lines like `exit=$LASTEXITCODE`.
